readings.subject: Complex-product classification for distribution of SFC-authorised funds within the retained circular
readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] The question answered is whether, for a fund within this circular’s scope at the assessment time, a ground requiring complex-product treatment for distribution is established under this circular. True means that either the fund’s total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to at least 50% of its NAV, or an applicable SFC case-by-case complex-product designation exists. False means that neither ground applies, provided both grounds have been resolved on adequate evidence; it does not establish that the fund is non-complex under every other applicable rule. An unresolved exposure calculation or designation status remains unknown and must not be supplied as false. The scope comprises funds authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong, excluding listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs). Private market assets here comprise private credit and private equity, reached directly or indirectly. Exactly 50% triggers mandatory classification; no separate discretionary decision is stated as necessary at that threshold. Below 50%, footnote 7 places the classification assessment within the SFC’s holistic, case-by-case discretion. The SFC may designate such a fund after considering its aggregate exposures, investment strategy, portfolio composition, liquidity and risk profile, particular asset types and structures, and home-regulator distribution conditions; these factors are non-exhaustive and do not individually establish designation. Once classified, the fund is subject to the prevailing complex-product sale requirements, expressly including suitability irrespective of solicitation or recommendation. Fund managers must address the classification in their distributor selection and communications. The source supplies neither a particular fund’s exposure calculation nor its designation record, so no particular fund’s classification is decided here.
readings.distinction: This is a classification-trigger predicate, not a Boolean finding of overall compliance, prohibition, licensing, or suitability. Mandatory classification at or above 50% is distinct from the SFC’s discretion to designate below 50%; discretion to make the designation does not make the resulting classification optional once an applicable designation exists. LAFs are excluded from this circular’s definition of Funds, rather than declared non-complex. The separate 15% direct-private-asset investment limit in footnote 1 does not replace the 50% combined-exposure threshold, excuse its application, or cap indirect exposures at 15%. Exposure-related disclosures, target-market duties, advertising requirements and authorisation scrutiny are separate from the classification trigger. Missing evidence of exposure or designation is an unresolved classification question, not evidence of an exemption or absence of designation.

citations.quote: This circular provides guidance to management companies of funds that are authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong (Funds)6 in this regard.
A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV.
On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:
In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.
7 In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.
6 Except for listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs).
including but not limited to ensuring the suitability of the Fund for its investors irrespective of whether solicitation or recommendation is involved.
1 Direct investments in/exposures to private assets fall within the investment limit of 15% of a Fund’s total net asset value (NAV) under 7.3 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds (UT Code).
Fund managers are encouraged to consult the SFC at the earliest opportunity if they are in doubt regarding complex product classification of their Funds.

assumptions: All facts refer to the same identified fund and assessment time. The retained text does not provide that time or establish the circular’s publication, commencement or transitional dates.

The formalization encodes the circular’s classification grounds only. It does not calculate exposures, predict an SFC discretionary decision, or encode the full distribution requirements incorporated by reference.

The exposure-threshold fact must be supplied from an adequately supported aggregate-exposure assessment. The source does not specify a complete look-through, valuation, netting, derivative-exposure or double-counting methodology, or resolve whether actual, permitted or intended exposure controls every assessment.

The SFC-designation fact concerns an actual applicable designation, not the presence of risk factors or the possibility that the SFC could designate the fund. Neither silence nor an unsuccessful search alone establishes its absence.
No prior reading was supplied. The uncertainties concerning exposure measurement, timing, external requirements and fund-specific evidence remain unresolved in this initial proposal.
questions: What fund and assessment date are at issue, and is the fund SFC-authorised for public offering in Hong Kong and outside the LAF exclusion?
What contemporaneous evidence establishes aggregate direct and indirect private-market exposure relative to NAV, and what measurement and look-through methodology governs that assessment?
Does an applicable SFC case-by-case designation exist, and what are its effective date, scope and any subsequent changes?
Does the governing classification practice assess actual holdings, permitted investment limits, intended exposure or a combination, and how are temporary threshold crossings treated?

facts.name: fund.sfc_authorised_public_hk
facts.meaning: Whether the identified fund is authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong at the assessment time. Supply from the applicable authorisation record; an unavailable record leaves the fact unknown.
facts.unit: Boolean authorisation-and-offering-scope status at the assessment time

facts.name: fund.is_laf
facts.meaning: Whether the identified fund is a listed closed-ended alternative asset fund within the LAF category excluded by footnote 6. Professional judgment may be needed to establish category membership using the separate LAF materials.
facts.unit: Boolean membership in the excluded LAF category

facts.name: fund.aggregate_private_exposure_at_least_half_nav
facts.meaning: Whether an adequately supported assessment establishes that the fund’s total direct and indirect exposures to private credit and private equity amount to at least 50% of its NAV at the relevant assessment time. Exactly 50% is true. A supported amount below 50% is false. Missing or unresolved classification, valuation or aggregation evidence leaves this fact unknown. This is a specific exposure-threshold input, not an overall classification or compliance conclusion.
facts.unit: Boolean threshold comparison; underlying exposure and NAV must use a consistent valuation basis, with the threshold equal to one half of NAV

facts.name: fund.applicable_sfc_discretionary_designation
facts.meaning: Whether an actual SFC case-by-case complex-product designation under this circular applies to the identified fund at the assessment time. The below-50% assessment is holistic and considers non-exhaustive factors. Those factors alone cannot supply true. False requires adequate evidence that no such designation applies; an unavailable designation history remains unknown. Professional judgment may be needed to interpret the scope and continuing applicability of a decision.
facts.unit: Boolean applicability of an actual SFC discretionary designation

dimensions.explanation: The classification rule concerns SFC-authorised funds offered to the public in Hong Kong, with LAFs excluded. Management companies are the guidance’s principal addressees; the SFC makes discretionary designations, and fund managers must select knowledgeable, appropriate distributors and communicate relevant changes. The circular separately addresses scrutiny of new authorisation applications and review of existing authorised funds. An applicant’s closer scrutiny is not itself an existing complex-product designation.

Private market assets expressly comprise private credit and private equity. Direct exposure includes the described lending or equity investments in unlisted companies; indirect examples include BDCs, CLOs and financial derivatives. Footnotes define BDCs and CLOs and illustrate TRSs and SRTs; the indirect examples are expressly non-exhaustive. The mandatory boundary is total direct and indirect exposure of at least 50% of NAV. The text does not fully specify how to measure that total, including look-through proportions, derivative amounts, overlapping exposures, or actual versus permitted exposure, so instrument names alone cannot settle a fund-specific threshold calculation.

LAFs are expressly outside this circular’s Fund definition and are referred to a separate circular. Below 50% is not an exemption from possible complex-product treatment: it is the setting identified in footnote 7 for discretionary designation. No exception to the mandatory at-least-50% rule is stated for an in-scope Fund. The 15% direct-investment limit is a separate constraint, not a classification exception. Exclusion here does not establish non-complex status under other rules.

‘Will be considered’ establishes mandatory classification at the numerical threshold; ‘may also designate’ reserves a holistic below-threshold decision to the SFC. The listed factors inform discretion and are neither exhaustive nor individually sufficient. Once classified, prevailing complex-product sale requirements apply, expressly including suitability without solicitation or recommendation. The general introductory ‘where appropriate’ does not displace the later express threshold. Existing-fund review is expected, while early consultation in cases of doubt is encouraged; neither wording supplies an exemption pending consultation.

The retained text supplies no issue date, commencement date, fixed transition deadline, exposure observation frequency, averaging period, or treatment of temporary crossings and later decreases. Existing funds are expected to review and act, including updating offering documents, as soon as practicable; consultation is encouraged at the earliest opportunity when classification is doubtful. Sale requirements are described as prevailing, and indirect-exposure examples may be updated from time to time. Footnote 9 dates the separate internal-product-approval guidance to 2014-04-30 and its update to 2016-03-04. Footnote 10 describes the advertising guidelines’ latest version as issued in April 2013, without a day. These are referenced-document dates, not this circular’s commencement date, and their present currency is not established by the packet.

Application requires fund-specific authorisation and LAF status, reliable exposure and NAV evidence, relevant SFC designation records and, for discretionary assessment, the fund’s characteristics and home-regulator conditions. Referenced texts not reproduced include UT Code paragraph 7.3, the LAF circular, Code of Conduct paragraph 5.5, Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms Guidelines Chapter 6 and relevant FAQs, internal-product-approval guidance and advertising guidelines. Their complete conditions and exceptions cannot be inferred. The packet also declares missing.7b393f53d503773a762cf757, missing.de6722b4a9f08d782e48c11a and missing.13ee048eabca24d91ac9305c with null source hashes but does not map them to particular references. Missing materials do not erase the retained express threshold, but prevent a complete account of external classification and distribution rules.

coverage.reason: Defines private market assets as private credit and private equity and identifies direct and indirect routes relevant to the aggregate threshold.
Identifies covered Funds and management-company addressees, distinguishes exposure-driven disclosures from possible scrutiny and classification, and incorporates the LAF footnote.
Explains illiquidity, valuation, credit, transparency and structural risks motivating the guidance. These concerns support contextual assessment but do not independently classify every exposed fund.
Requires attention to clear, complete and balanced risk information and appropriate distributors; those responsibilities are distinct from satisfying a classification ground.
The enhanced-disclosure heading separates the ensuing offering-document requirements from the later designation rule.
Possible direct or indirect exposure triggers the stated disclosure guidance, including the KFS, without requiring the 50% classification threshold.
Requires disclosure of exposure extent and access routes. Its illustrative percentage ranges are not additional classification thresholds or a complete calculation method.
Requires disclosure of underlying-asset characteristics, such as CLO ratings and TRS reference assets, which can inform exposure assessment without mechanically resolving classification.
Requires asset-specific risk disclosures and implications in offering documents and, where appropriate, the KFS. Valuation-risk disclosure is separate from the classification decision.
The complex-product-designation heading identifies the provisions directly answering the selected question.
Establishes automatic complex-product classification at aggregate exposure of 50% or more of NAV and a separate SFC case-by-case designation power.
Aggregate exposure remains a discretionary assessment factor below the automatic threshold, rather than becoming irrelevant below 50%.
Strategy, portfolio composition, liquidity and risk profile inform holistic discretion; no individual factor is stated to compel designation.
Asset extent, nature and characteristics, including CLO tranches and ratings and SRT structures and underlying assets, inform discretion without supplying standalone numerical tests.
Home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements and other conditions are relevant factors. Their existence, contents and weight require case-specific evidence.
Requires a holistic assessment of the specific circumstances; footnote 7 confines the described discretionary assessment to aggregate exposure below 50%.

States the consequence of classification: prevailing complex-product sale requirements, expressly including suitability regardless of solicitation or recommendation. It is not a separate exposure trigger.
The target-market and distributor-selection heading identifies related implementation responsibilities rather than another classification threshold.
Reminds managers to observe external internal-product-approval guidance on target markets and distributors. Its complete requirements are not reproduced.

Managers must address target-market understanding, needs and risk appetite and select distributors able to understand complex status, assign an appropriate risk rating where applicable and advise investors. A risk rating is not a substitute for the circular’s classification grounds.
Marketing materials must meet the incorporated advertising guidelines, including balance and adequate risk disclosures; advertising compliance does not determine complex-product status.
The ‘Others’ heading introduces authorisation scrutiny and existing-fund implementation provisions.
New funds with possible exposure may receive closer scrutiny and may not use FASTrack. Neither possibility is equivalent to designation, and FASTrack treatment is not a classification exception.

Existing-fund managers are expected to review, act, update documents as soon as practicable and communicate with distributors. Early SFC consultation is encouraged for classification doubt. The reference to paragraphs 9 and 10 is retained, but the packet does not provide original paragraph-number mapping.
Identifies relevant case officers as a clarification route; it does not create a waiver, exception or presumption pending a response.
Identifies the Investment Products Division as the issuing division.
Identifies the SFC as the issuing authority and actor exercising the designation discretion.

Footnote 1 places direct private-asset exposure within the separate 15% NAV investment limit under UT Code paragraph 7.3. It neither replaces the combined 50% threshold nor supplies the missing full UT Code conditions.
Footnote 2 makes indirect-exposure examples non-exhaustive and subject to SFC updates, preventing an inference that unlisted examples are excluded.

Footnote 3 describes BDCs as close-ended funds registered under the US Investment Company Act of 1940, primarily investing in debt and equity of small and mid-sized US companies. This informs instrument identification but does not establish a particular fund’s exposure amount.

Footnote 4 describes CLOs as debt-pool-backed securities, typically involving leveraged or broadly syndicated loans or direct lending to unlisted companies. Holding a CLO does not alone establish the aggregate threshold.
Footnote 5 includes TRSs on loan-exposed indices and SRTs backed by corporate loans as derivative examples. Their classification and measurement need underlying evidence.
Footnote 6 expressly excludes LAFs and refers them to a separate circular. That circular’s contents are absent, so LAF treatment cannot be decided here.
Footnote 7 expressly identifies less-than-50% exposure as the setting for the holistic designation assessment. This preserves the distinction from mandatory classification at exactly 50% or above.

Footnote 8 identifies Code of Conduct paragraph 5.5, Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms Guidelines Chapter 6 and relevant FAQs. Their full text and any applicable conditions or exceptions are missing; only the retained express sale consequence can be stated.
Footnote 9 identifies the external internal-product-approval guidance as issued on 2014-04-30 and updated on 2016-03-04. These dates do not establish the retained circular’s effective date.
Footnote 10 identifies an April 2013 version of the external advertising guidelines. The packet does not supply a day, the full guidelines or independent evidence of their present currency.

questions: What are the retained circular’s issue and commencement dates, and are there applicable transitional provisions or subsequent amendments?

Which exposure methodology governs look-through holdings, derivatives, valuation, overlapping exposures and actual versus permitted exposure, and what evidence supports the particular fund’s calculation?
What do the fund’s authorisation record, LAF classification evidence and SFC designation history establish at the relevant assessment time?
What are the full applicable provisions of the referenced complex-product sale rules and FAQs, UT Code paragraph 7.3, LAF circular, internal-product-approval guidance and advertising guidelines?
Which referenced materials correspond to the three missing dependency identifiers, and can their absent source hashes and contents be supplied?
How are temporary threshold crossings, subsequent exposure reductions and the duration or withdrawal of a discretionary designation treated?
